finalText:
I worked all 16 open RMAs. I closed 12, left 3 open and put 1 under investigation. One date conflict: your prompt says today is 2026-10-12, but the return policy and order data say 2026-07-25. I used 2026-07-25 for the return windows.

**Closed (refunded and restocked):**
- **RMA-801:** Card refund of 10,965 (15% fee). The keyboard went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-802:** Card refund of 15,900. There is no fee because the request fell in the PU-21 window (10–20 July). The headphones went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-803 and RMA-804:** Each got 27,965 as store credit (15% fee). Both were requested 41 days after shipping, and neither customer held gold or platinum on the request date. C-803 only became gold on 15 July. I recorded each refund against its order and added the same amount to the customer's balance. Both monitors went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-805:** Card refund of 5,520, with the 20% fee that applied to requests made in May–June (PU-15). The hub went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-806:** Card refund of 7,350, no fee because the mice were defective. Both mice went into the damaged bucket.
- **RMA-810:** Card refund of 9,900, which is the 12,900 paid less the 3,000 already refunded. The keyboard went into the damaged bucket.
- **RMA-811:** Card refund of 4,900, no fee because the mouse was damaged in transit. The warehouse graded it resellable, so it went into sellable stock.
- **RMA-812:** Card refund of 21,900, no fee because the dock was defective. The dock went into the damaged bucket.
- **RMA-813:** Card refund of 10,965 (15% fee). The request came exactly 30 days after shipping, which is inside the window. The keyboard went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-814:** Card refund of 31,800 with no fee (PU-21). Both pairs arrived in separate parcels and went back to sellable stock.
- **RMA-815:** Card refund of 10,965 (15% fee). The request came 38 days after shipping, but the customer is platinum, so the 45-day window applies (PU-18). The keyboard went back to sellable stock.

**Left open:**
- **RMA-809:** The warehouse has received 2 of the 3 cables, one resellable and one damaged. I refunded those 2 units (3,800, no fee under PU-21) and restocked them, one sellable and one damaged. The RMA stays open for the third cable.
- **RMA-807 and RMA-816:** The warehouse has received nothing against either one. I refunded and restocked nothing. The RMA-807 customer says the parcel reached the warehouse, but that doesn't count until the warehouse records it.

**Investigation:**
- **RMA-808:** The warehouse received a cable (P-CAB) instead of the monitor (P-MON) the return covers. I opened investigation INV-1 and refunded and restocked nothing.

I didn't contact any customers, because the task didn't cover it.
